formulas.title: Thiele Equation for Current-Driven Skyrmion Motion
formulas.description: Describes the steady-state rigid-body drift velocity $\mathbf{v}_d$ of a magnetic skyrmion driven by spin-polarized current drift velocity $\mathbf{v}_s$ under the balance of topological Magnus force, Gilbert damping, non-adiabatic spin-transfer torque, and defect pinning force $\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{pin}}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Thiele equation projects the continuum Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics onto collective center-of-mass coordinates, coupling skyrmion topology directly to transverse Magnus deflection and dissipative drag.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A driven skyrmion moves like a spinning top sliding across a rough table: its topological spin creates a sideways Magnus force that lets it curve smoothly around obstacles instead of getting stuck like a rigid domain wall.
formulas.interpretation: The first term $\mathbf{G} \times (\mathbf{v}_s - \mathbf{v}_d)$ is the topological Magnus force proportional to the winding number $Q$, the second term $\mathcal{D}(\beta \mathbf{v}_s - \alpha \mathbf{v}_d)$ balances non-adiabatic drive against Gilbert dissipation, and $\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{pin}}$ accounts for disorder potentials. Because the Magnus term dominates over small damping $\alpha \ll 1$, skyrmions deflect around pinning centers and depin at currents near $10^6\,\mathrm{A/m^2}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived from translational Goldstone-mode projection of the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation under broken continuous two-dimensional translational symmetry of the localized soliton core.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Assumes a rigid, undeformed skyrmion profile moving at sub-critical velocities well below core-distortion or magnon-emission thresholds. In the Galilean-invariant limit $\beta = \alpha$ with $\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{pin}} = 0$, the equation yields exact co-moving drift $\mathbf{v}_d = \mathbf{v}_s$.

\\mathbf{G}.name: Gyrocoupling Vector
\\mathbf{G}.description: Out-of-plane topological gyrocoupling vector $\mathbf{G} = (M_s t / \gamma) 4\pi Q \hat{\mathbf{z}}$ proportional to the skyrmion winding number $Q$.

\\mathbf{v}_s.name: Conduction Electron Spin-Drift Velocity
\\mathbf{v}_s.description: Effective spin-polarized electron drift velocity proportional to the applied electrical current density $\mathbf{j}$.

\\mathbf{v}_d.name: Skyrmion Drift Velocity
\\mathbf{v}_d.description: Steady-state center-of-mass translational velocity of the moving magnetic skyrmion.

\\mathcal{D}.name: Dissipative Tensor Coefficient
\\mathcal{D}.description: Isotropic diagonal component of the Thiele dissipation dyadic encoding spin-texture gradient damping.

\\beta.name: Non-Adiabatic Spin-Transfer Torque Parameter
\\beta.description: Dimensionless parameter quantifying dissipative non-adiabatic momentum transfer from conduction electrons to the magnetization texture.

\\alpha.name: Gilbert Damping Constant
\\alpha.description: Dimensionless phenomenological damping parameter governing magnetization energy relaxation.

\\mathbf{F}_{\\mathrm{pin}}.name: Pinning Force
\\mathbf{F}_{\\mathrm{pin}}.description: Restoring force exerted on the skyrmion core by crystalline impurities, grain boundaries, or thickness variations.

formulas.title: Skyrmion Hall Angle
formulas.description: Gives the tangent of the transverse deflection angle $\theta_{\mathrm{SkH}}$ between the skyrmion drift velocity $\mathbf{v}_d$ and the driving spin-current direction $\mathbf{v}_s$ in the depinned steady-state regime.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The skyrmion Hall angle $\theta_{\mathrm{SkH}}$ quantifies the topological Magnus deflection of a current-driven skyrmion away from the applied current axis, reversing sign with topological charge $Q$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Because a skyrmion has nonzero topological spin $G$, pushing it straight forward with an electric current makes it veer diagonally to the left or right unless damping $\alpha$ and non-adiabatic torque $\beta$ match or opposite skyrmions cancel their charge.
formulas.interpretation: Solving the pinning-free Thiele equation for $\mathbf{v}_s$ along the $x$-axis yields longitudinal velocity $v_x = (\alpha \beta \mathcal{D}^2 + G^2)/(\alpha^2 \mathcal{D}^2 + G^2) v_s$ and transverse velocity $v_y = (\alpha - \beta) \mathcal{D} G / (\alpha^2 \mathcal{D}^2 + G^2) v_s$, whose ratio gives $\tan \theta_{\mathrm{SkH}}$. In synthetic antiferromagnets pairing $Q = +1$ and $Q = -1$ skyrmions, the net gyrocoupling $G$ cancels to zero and eliminates transverse drift.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from the broken chiral mirror symmetry of the topological Magnus force $\mathbf{G} \times (\mathbf{v}_s - \mathbf{v}_d)$ whenever the net winding number $Q \neq 0$ and $\alpha \neq \beta$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Vanishes identically when $G = 0$ (topologically trivial bubbles or compensated antiferromagnetic skyrmions) or when $\alpha = \beta$. In the pure adiabatic limit $\beta \to 0$, the expression simplifies to $\tan \theta_{\mathrm{SkH}} = \alpha \mathcal{D} / G$.

\\theta_{\\mathrm{SkH}}.name: Skyrmion Hall Angle

formulas.title: Three-Dimensional Weyl Fermion Hamiltonian
formulas.description: Effective low-energy two-band Hamiltonian describing linearly dispersing bulk quasiparticles near an isolated three-dimensional Weyl node of positive or negative chirality at momentum displacement $\mathbf{q}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Weyl Hamiltonian $H_{\pm}(\mathbf{q}) = \pm \hbar v_F \boldsymbol{\sigma} \cdot \mathbf{q}$ couples the three Pauli matrices $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ linearly to all three components of the momentum offset $\mathbf{q}$, producing a gapless conical spectrum whose pseudospin is strictly locked parallel or antiparallel to momentum.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Near a Weyl touching point in a three-dimensional crystal, electrons behave like massless relativistic particles whose internal spin-like degree of freedom points strictly along or opposite to their direction of motion, making the crossing impossible to erase with small perturbations.
formulas.interpretation: Because $H_{\pm}(\mathbf{q})$ is a $2 \times 2$ Hermitian matrix that already utilizes all three traceless Pauli matrices $\sigma_x, \sigma_y, \sigma_z$, any small perturbation $\delta H = \mathbf{m} \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma}$ merely shifts the node location in momentum space to $\mathbf{q} = \mp \mathbf{m}/(\hbar v_F)$ rather than opening an energy gap. Its eigenvalues $E(\mathbf{q}) = \pm \hbar v_F |\mathbf{q}|$ form an isotropic three-dimensional cone, while the overall sign $\pm$ fixes the helicity and topological chirality of the node.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from $\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{p}$ expansion around an accidental two-fold band degeneracy in a three-dimensional crystal where either spatial inversion ($\mathcal{P}$) or time-reversal ($\mathcal{T}$) symmetry is broken so that Kramers degeneracy is lifted.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: As $\mathbf{q} \to \mathbf{0}$, the valence and conduction bands meet at a point of vanishing density of states $g(E) \propto E^2$. At larger momentum displacements away from the node, higher-order lattice dispersion terms curve the cones and eventually merge opposite-chirality valleys at a Lifshitz transition.

H_{\\pm}(\\mathbf{q}).name: Weyl Effective Hamiltonian
H_{\\pm}(\\mathbf{q}).description: Two-by-two Hermitian effective Hamiltonian matrix governing low-energy Bloch states near a Weyl node of chirality $\pm 1$.

\\mathbf{q}.description: Three-dimensional crystal wavevector measured relative to the Weyl node position $\mathbf{k}_0$ in the Brillouin zone.

formulas.title: Weyl Node Berry Curvature Monopole
formulas.description: Gives the radial momentum-space Berry curvature field generated around an isolated three-dimensional Weyl node, taking the exact inverse-square form of a Dirac magnetic monopole located at $\mathbf{q} = \mathbf{0}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Berry curvature $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{\pm}(\mathbf{q}) = \pm \mathbf{q}/(2q^3)$ measures the local geometric phase flux per unit area in three-dimensional momentum space surrounding a Weyl degeneracy, diverging as $q^{-2}$ at the nodal singularity.
formulas.intuitive_summary: In crystal momentum space, a Weyl node acts like an isolated north or south magnetic monopole whose invisible geometric force field radiates outward or inward with an inverse-square law, deflecting electron wavepackets sideways.
formulas.interpretation: Evaluating $\boldsymbol{\Omega}(\mathbf{q}) = \nabla_{\mathbf{q}} \times \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{q})$ for the conduction-band eigenstate of $H_{\pm}(\mathbf{q}) = \pm \hbar v_F \boldsymbol{\sigma} \cdot \mathbf{q}$ yields a purely radial pseudovector field independent of the Fermi velocity $v_F$. Its divergence vanishes everywhere away from the origin but equals a Dirac delta function $\nabla_{\mathbf{q}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{\pm} = \pm 2\pi \delta^{(3)}(\mathbf{q})$ at the node, directly driving anomalous transverse velocities in semiclassical electron dynamics.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from the $U(1)$ phase geometry of the two-component Bloch spinor fiber bundle over the punctured momentum space $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \{\mathbf{0}\}$, whose first Chern class on any surrounding sphere is non-trivial.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: As $q \to 0$, $|\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{\pm}(\mathbf{q})|$ diverges as $1/(2q^2)$, signaling the exact band degeneracy where the adiabatic single-band approximation breaks down. As $q \to \infty$, the monopole field decays as $q^{-2}$ until contributions from neighboring Weyl nodes dominate.

\\boldsymbol{\\Omega}_{\\pm}(\\mathbf{q}.name: Momentum-Space Berry Curvature
\\boldsymbol{\\Omega}_{\\pm}(\\mathbf{q}.description: Pseudovector Berry curvature field in three-dimensional reciprocal space generated by a Weyl node of chirality $\pm 1$.

\\mathbf{q}.name: Momentum Displacement Wavevector
\\mathbf{q}.description: Three-dimensional wavevector offset measured from the Weyl touching point.

formulas.title: Weyl Node Topological Chirality
formulas.description: Defines the quantized topological chirality $\chi = \pm 1$ of an isolated Weyl node as the first Chern number obtained by integrating the Berry curvature flux over any closed surface $S^2$ enclosing the node in three-dimensional momentum space.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The surface integral $\chi = \frac{1}{2\pi} \oint_{S^2} \boldsymbol{\Omega}(\mathbf{k}) \cdot d\mathbf{S}$ assigns an integer topological invariant to any isolated band crossing in the Brillouin zone, certifying its robustness against smooth Hamiltonian deformations.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Wrapping an imaginary bubble around a Weyl node in momentum space and counting the total Berry curvature lines piercing outward always yields exactly $+1$ or $-1$, a locked integer charge that cannot change continuously.
formulas.interpretation: Because the Bloch states are smooth and gapped everywhere on the closed Fermi sphere $S^2$ surrounding the node, the total Berry flux is quantized to integer multiples of $2\pi$ by the Gauss-Bonnet and Chern theorems. For a linear Weyl crossing, $\chi = +1$ denotes a right-handed Berry-curvature source and $\chi = -1$ denotes a left-handed sink; higher-order multi-Weyl nodes protected by crystal rotation symmetries can carry $|\chi| = 2$ or $3$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Quantization is guaranteed by the second cohomology group $H^2(S^2, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}$ classifying complex line bundles over the enclosing momentum-space two-sphere.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: The integral is strictly independent of the radius or geometric distortion of $S^2$ as long as no other band degeneracy crosses the surface. If a Weyl node merges with an opposite-chirality partner inside $S^2$, the net enclosed flux drops discontinuously to $\chi = 0$ and a band gap can open.

\\chi.name: Weyl Node Chirality
\\chi.description: Quantized integer topological charge (Chern number) distinguishing right-handed ($+1$) and left-handed ($-1$) Weyl nodes.

\\boldsymbol{\\Omega}(\\mathbf{k}).name: Momentum-Space Berry Curvature
\\boldsymbol{\\Omega}(\\mathbf{k}).description: Berry curvature pseudovector evaluated on the gapped two-dimensional surface enclosing the band crossing.

d\\mathbf{S}.name: Momentum-Space Surface Area Element
d\\mathbf{S}.description: Outward-directed infinitesimal area vector on the closed momentum-space sphere $S^2$ surrounding the Weyl node.

formulas.title: Nielsen-Ninomiya Fermion-Doubling Theorem
formulas.description: States that the sum of topological chiralities $\chi_i$ over all isolated Weyl nodes inside the periodic three-dimensional Brillouin zone of any local lattice Hamiltonian must equal zero.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Chirality neutrality $\sum_i \chi_i = 0$ enforces global topological charge conservation on the compact Brillouin torus $T^3$, proving that right-handed and left-handed Weyl fermions must always occur in equal numbers in any crystal.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Because a crystal's momentum space wraps back on itself with no edges, every magnetic-monopole source of Berry curvature must be balanced by an equal sink somewhere else, so Weyl nodes can never appear solo.
formulas.interpretation: Applying the divergence theorem to the Berry curvature across the entire periodic Brillouin zone $T^3$—which has no boundary—forces the sum of all monopole residues to vanish identically. Consequently, the minimal number of Weyl nodes is two in a time-reversal-broken, inversion-symmetric crystal, and four in a time-reversal-symmetric, inversion-broken crystal where time reversal maps a node at $\mathbf{k}_0$ to another node of the same chirality at $-\mathbf{k}_0$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from the compact, boundaryless topology of the three-dimensional Brillouin torus $T^3$ imposed by discrete lattice translation invariance.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Holds strictly for any local, short-ranged periodic lattice model in three dimensions. The theorem can be evaded only on the three-dimensional boundary of a four-dimensional topological insulator, where a single unpaired chiral fermion can reside on one surface while its partner lives on the opposite boundary.

\\chi_i.name: Individual Weyl Node Chirality
\\chi_i.description: Quantized integer Chern number ($\pm 1$) of the $i$-th isolated Weyl node inside the first Brillouin zone.

formulas.title: Weyl Semimetal Anomalous Hall Conductivity
formulas.description: Relates the intrinsic zero-field anomalous Hall conductivity $\sigma_{xy}$ of a minimal time-reversal-broken Weyl semimetal directly to the momentum-space separation $\Delta k_z$ between its opposite-chirality Weyl nodes.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The intrinsic Hall conductivity $\sigma_{xy} = \frac{e^2}{2\pi h} \Delta k_z$ measures the integrated Berry curvature dipole across the Brillouin zone, quantifying how each two-dimensional momentum slice between the two Weyl nodes contributes one conductance quantum $e^2/h$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A magnetic Weyl semimetal behaves like a stack of two-dimensional quantum Hall layers packed into momentum space between its two Weyl nodes, so the farther apart the nodes sit, the stronger the transverse Hall voltage becomes.
formulas.interpretation: Treating the wavevector component $k_z$ as a tuning parameter, every two-dimensional slice $k_z \in (-\Delta k_z/2, +\Delta k_z/2)$ is a gapped Chern insulator carrying Hall conductance $e^2/h$, whereas slices outside this window have zero Chern number. Integrating over $k_z$ with measure $dk_z/(2\pi)$ yields a semi-quantized bulk conductivity proportional solely to the node separation $\Delta k_z$, providing a direct transport measure of the Berry-curvature dipole.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Requires broken time-reversal symmetry ($\mathcal{T}$), since $\mathcal{T}$ enforces $\boldsymbol{\Omega}(-\mathbf{k}) = -\boldsymbol{\Omega}(\mathbf{k})$ and forces the Brillouin-zone integral of $\Omega_z(\mathbf{k})$ to vanish identically.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: As $\Delta k_z \to 0$, the opposite-chirality nodes merge into a Dirac point and $\sigma_{xy} \to 0$. When $\Delta k_z$ expands across the entire Brillouin zone to equal the reciprocal lattice vector $G_z = 2\pi/c$, the nodes annihilate at the zone boundary and the system becomes a three-dimensional quantum anomalous Hall insulator with $\sigma_{xy} = e^2/(hc)$.

\\sigma_{xy}.name: Anomalous Hall Conductivity
\\sigma_{xy}.description: Intrinsic transverse electrical conductivity in the $xy$-plane arising from bulk Berry curvature without an external magnetic field.

h.name: Planck Constant

\\Delta k_z.name: Weyl Node Momentum Separation
\\Delta k_z.description: Separation along the $k_z$-axis in reciprocal space between a pair of opposite-chirality Weyl nodes.

formulas.title: Chiral Anomaly Charge Pumping Rate
formulas.description: Describes the non-conservation of chiral carrier number density $\rho_5 = n_+ - n_-$ in a Weyl semimetal under parallel electric and magnetic fields $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{B}$, balanced by intervalley relaxation time $\tau_v$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The chiral anomaly balance equation $\partial_t \rho_5 = \frac{e^2}{2\pi^2 \hbar^2} \mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B} - \rho_5 / \tau_v$ quantifies the quantum-mechanical pumping of electrons between opposite-chirality Weyl valleys via the gapless zeroth Landau level.
formulas.intuitive_summary: When electric and magnetic fields point in the same direction through a Weyl crystal, quantum mechanics opens a one-way conveyor belt that pumps electrons out of left-handed valleys and into right-handed valleys until large-momentum scattering restores balance.
formulas.interpretation: In a magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, the Landau degeneracy per unit transverse area is $eB/(2\pi\hbar)$, while a parallel electric field accelerates states along the chiral zeroth Landau level at rate $\dot{k}_{\parallel} = eE/\hbar$. Multiplying these factors gives a valley pumping rate proportional to $\mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B}$ that creates a steady-state chiral imbalance $\rho_5 = \frac{e^2 \tau_v}{2\pi^2 \hbar^2} \mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B}$, driving negative longitudinal magnetoresistance proportional to $B^2 \cos^2\theta$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Manifests the Adler-Bell-Jackiw axial anomaly of $3+1$ dimensional quantum electrodynamics, in which classical chiral $U(1)_A$ symmetry cannot be preserved simultaneously with electromagnetic $U(1)_V$ gauge invariance upon quantization.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: When $\mathbf{E} \perp \mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B} = 0$ and chiral pumping vanishes identically, recovering ordinary positive orbital magnetoresistance. In the clean limit $\tau_v \to \infty$, the chiral imbalance grows linearly in time without saturation until nonlinear band dispersion intervenes.

\\rho_5.name: Chiral Carrier Number Density
\\rho_5.description: Difference $n_+ - n_-$ between the electron number densities occupying right-handed and left-handed Weyl valleys.

e.name: Elementary Charge
e.description: Magnitude of the electron charge coupling carriers to external electromagnetic fields.

\\tau_v.description: Relaxation time required for large-momentum impurity or phonon scattering to transfer carriers between opposite-chirality Weyl nodes.

formulas.title: Chiral Magnetic Effect Current Density
formulas.description: Expresses the electrical current density $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{CME}}$ flowing parallel to an applied magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$ when a non-equilibrium chiral chemical potential imbalance $\mu_5 = (\mu_+ - \mu_-)/2$ separates opposite-chirality Weyl nodes.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The chiral magnetic current $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{CME}} = \frac{e^2}{2\pi^2 \hbar^2} \mu_5 \mathbf{B}$ represents a non-dissipative transport response along $\mathbf{B}$ driven by unequal occupation of right-handed and left-handed chiral Landau levels.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Once more electrons pile up in right-handed Weyl valleys than in left-handed ones, an applied magnetic field guides those unbalanced chiral channels into a net electrical current flowing straight along the magnetic field lines.
formulas.interpretation: In the zeroth Landau level, right-handed electrons move parallel to $\mathbf{B}$ while left-handed electrons move antiparallel. Whenever a chiral anomaly pump establishes a non-equilibrium chemical potential difference $\mu_5$ between valleys, the two opposing currents fail to cancel, producing a macroscopic current density proportional to $\mu_5 \mathbf{B}$ that directly yields the positive $B^2$ longitudinal magnetoconductivity observed in Weyl semimetals.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Protected by the same topological anomaly coefficient $e^2/(2\pi^2 \hbar^2)$ as the Adler-Bell-Jackiw chiral anomaly, while global Bloch-theorem energy minimization guarantees that $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{CME}}$ vanishes strictly in static thermal equilibrium when $\mu_5$ is purely an energy offset between nodes.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: When valley populations equilibrate ($\mu_5 \to 0$) or the magnetic field vanishes ($\mathbf{B} \to \mathbf{0}$), $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{CME}} \to \mathbf{0}$. At ultra-high fields in the extreme quantum limit where only the zeroth Landau level is occupied, the prefactor remains exact while $\mu_5$ depends linearly on the chiral density $\rho_5$ through the $B$-dependent density of states.

\\mathbf{j}_{\\mathrm{CME}}.name: Chiral Magnetic Current Density
\\mathbf{j}_{\\mathrm{CME}}.description: Electrical current density generated parallel to the magnetic field by a non-equilibrium chiral chemical potential imbalance.

\\hbar.name: Reduced Planck Constant
\\hbar.description: Reduced Planck constant governing the Landau-level degeneracy and chiral anomaly prefactor.

formulas.title: Landau-Level Filling Factor
formulas.description: Defines the dimensionless Landau-level filling factor $\nu$ as the ratio of two-dimensional electron density $n$ to the magnetic flux-quantum density $B/\Phi_0$, equivalently expressed via the magnetic length $\ell_B = \sqrt{\hbar/(eB)}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The filling factor $\nu = n\Phi_0/B = 2\pi\ell_B^2 n$ counts the average number of electrons per magnetic flux quantum threading a two-dimensional electron gas, classifying integer and fractional quantum Hall states.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Each magnetic flux quantum piercing a two-dimensional electron sheet creates one available orbital slot per Landau level; the filling factor $\nu$ tells you how many electrons occupy each slot on average.
formulas.interpretation:
In a perpendicular magnetic field $B$, cyclotron quantization collapses the planar continuum into Landau levels of areal degeneracy $n_\Phi = B/\Phi_0 = (2\pi\ell_B^2)^{-1}$, where $\Phi_0 = h/e$. When $
u$ is an integer, an exact number of Landau levels are filled; when $
u < 1$, electrons reside solely in the lowest Landau level and share identical kinetic energy, allowing Coulomb interactions to stabilize incompressible fractional states at rational fillings such as $
u = 1/3$ and $2/5$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from magnetic translation invariance of a two-dimensional charged fluid in a uniform perpendicular magnetic field, which quantizes the area per orbital state to $2\pi\ell_B^2$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary:
As $B 	o \infty$ at fixed density $n$, $
u 	o 0$ and the system enters the ultra-quantum limit where classical Wigner crystallization eventually competes with fractional liquid phases near $
u \lesssim 1/7$. In the semiclassical limit $
u \gg 1$, many Landau levels are occupied and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations supersede discrete Hall plateaus.

\\nu.name: Landau-Level Filling Factor
\\nu.description: Dimensionless ratio of areal electron density to the orbital degeneracy of a single spin-polarized Landau level.

\\ell_B.description: Characteristic quantum cyclotron length scale $\sqrt{\hbar/(eB)}$ setting the spatial extent of lowest-Landau-level wavefunctions.

formulas.title: Lowest-Landau-Level Coulomb Energy Scale
formulas.description: Quantifies the characteristic electrostatic interaction energy $E_C$ between electrons separated by one magnetic length $\ell_B$ inside a host dielectric of permittivity $\varepsilon$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Because kinetic energy is quenched to a constant within a single Landau level, $E_C = e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon\ell_B)$ sets the sole intrinsic energy scale governing fractional quantum Hall excitation gaps and correlation energies.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Once a strong magnetic field freezes all electrons into the same kinetic-energy ring, the only energy scale left is how strongly two electrons repel each other at a spacing of one magnetic length $\ell_B$.
formulas.interpretation: In a GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure ($\varepsilon \approx 12.9\,\varepsilon_0$), $E_C$ scales as $\sqrt{B}$ (roughly $50\sqrt{B\,[\text{T}]}\,\text{K}$), whereas the cyclotron gap $\hbar\omega_c$ scales linearly with $B$. The ratio $\kappa = E_C/(\hbar\omega_c) \propto B^{-1/2}$ measures Landau-level mixing; at high magnetic fields $\kappa < 1$, projecting the Coulomb Hamiltonian purely onto the lowest Landau level becomes quantitatively accurate, and the $\nu = 1/3$ Laughlin gap evaluates to approximately $0.10\,E_C$ before finite-well-width and disorder reductions.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Determined by three-dimensional electrostatic Coulomb invariance projected onto a two-dimensional plane whose characteristic spatial metric is fixed by the magnetic length $\ell_B$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: In the infinite-field limit $B \to \infty$, $E_C/(\hbar\omega_c) \to 0$ and Landau-level mixing vanishes cleanly. When thermal energy $k_B T$ or disorder broadening exceeds the fractional gap $\sim 0.05\,E_C$, the incompressible fractional Hall plateau melts into a compressible metallic phase.

E_C.description: Characteristic electrostatic repulsion energy between two electrons separated by one magnetic length in the host semiconductor.

\\varepsilon.description: Absolute static permittivity $\varepsilon_r \varepsilon_0$ of the semiconductor host medium screening Coulomb interactions.

formulas.title: Laughlin Incompressible Fluid Wavefunction
formulas.description: Describes the correlated $N$-electron variational ground state $\Psi_m$ in the lowest Landau level at odd-denominator filling factor $\nu = 1/m$, where $z_j = x_j + i y_j$ are complex planar coordinates.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Laughlin's trial wavefunction $\Psi_m$ constructs an incompressible, rotationally invariant quantum liquid in the lowest Landau level by attaching $m$-fold holomorphic zeros to every electron pair to minimize short-range Coulomb repulsion.
formulas.intuitive_summary: By forcing the many-electron wavefunction to vanish as the $m$-th power whenever any two electrons approach each other, Laughlin's state keeps electrons maximally apart inside the lowest Landau level and locks them into a rigid topological fluid.
formulas.interpretation: Every factor $(z_j - z_k)^m$ is strictly analytic in $z_j$, guaranteeing that $\Psi_m$ lies entirely within the lowest Landau level, while odd integer $m$ enforces fermionic antisymmetry under particle exchange $z_j \leftrightarrow z_k$. The maximum single-particle angular momentum is $m(N-1)$, enclosing an area $2\pi\ell_B^2 m N$ and fixing the bulk density to $\nu = 1/m$. Numerical exact diagonalization of finite clusters confirms overlaps exceeding 99 percent with the true Coulomb ground state at $\nu = 1/3$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Selected by simultaneous invariance under planar rotations about the origin (total angular momentum $L = mN(N-1)/2$), fermionic exchange antisymmetry for odd $m$, and holomorphic projection onto the lowest Landau level.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: At $m = 1$, $\Psi_1$ reduces identically to the Vandermonde Slater determinant of a completely filled integer Landau level ($\nu = 1$). For $m \ge 7$, the corresponding classical plasma freezes into a triangular Wigner crystal, signaling the breakdown of the Laughlin liquid at very low fillings.

\\Psi_m.name: Laughlin Many-Body Wavefunction
\\Psi_m.description: Unnormalized $N$-electron probability amplitude for the incompressible fractional quantum Hall fluid at filling $\nu = 1/m$.

z_j.name: Complex Electron Coordinate
z_j.description: Two-dimensional position $x_j + i y_j$ of the $j$-th electron in the symmetric gauge.

m.description: Odd positive integer ($m = 1, 3, 5, \dots$) specifying the relative angular momentum of every electron pair and the inverse filling factor $1/\nu$.

N.name: Electron Number
N.description: Total number of spin-polarized electrons participating in the correlated many-body state.

\\ell_B.name: Magnetic Length
\\ell_B.description: Magnetic length $\sqrt{\hbar/(eB)}$ governing the Gaussian confinement envelope in the lowest Landau level.

formulas.title: Laughlin Quasihole Fractional Charge
formulas.description: Gives the quantized fractional electric charge $e^*$ of an elementary quasihole or quasiparticle excitation in a Laughlin fractional quantum Hall fluid at filling factor $\nu = 1/m$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Threading one magnetic flux quantum adiabatically through an incompressible $\nu = 1/m$ fluid creates a localized density deficit carrying an exact fraction $e^* = e/m$ of the elementary electron charge.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Pushing a single magnetic flux quantum into the $\nu = 1/m$ electron liquid expels exactly one $m$-th of an electron from that spot, leaving behind a stable, mobile quasiparticle with charge $e/m$.
formulas.interpretation: In Laughlin's plasma analogy, inserting a quasihole factor $\prod_j (z_j - z_0)$ adds a phantom impurity of unit charge to a plasma of charge-$m$ particles; Debye screening restores neutrality by displacing $1/m$ of a plasma particle, producing a real charge deficit of $+e/m$. Combining $m$ identical quasiholes reconstructs a single missing electron. Shot-noise measurements across weakly pinched quantum point contacts directly resolve $e^* = e/3$ at $\nu = 1/3$ and $e/5$ at $\nu = 2/5$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Protected by electromagnetic $U(1)$ gauge invariance and the quantized Hall conductance $\sigma_{xy} = e^2/(mh)$, which fixes the charge pumped per adiabatically inserted flux quantum $\Phi_0 = h/e$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: At $m = 1$ (integer quantum Hall state), $e^* = e$ recovers ordinary electronic hole excitations. In general Jain states $\nu = p/(2sp \pm 1)$, the fundamental quasiparticle charge generalizes to $e^* = e/(2sp \pm 1)$.

e^*.name: Quasiparticle Fractional Charge
e^*.description: Magnitude of the quantized electric charge carried by an elementary localized excitation of the Laughlin fluid.

e.name: Elementary Charge
e.description: Fundamental charge of a single electron ($1.602 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$).

m.description: Odd integer exponent characterizing the incompressible Laughlin state at filling $\nu = 1/m$.

formulas.title: Laughlin Anyon Exchange Braiding Phase
formulas.description: Specifies the topological statistical phase $\theta$ acquired by the many-body wavefunction when two identical Laughlin quasiholes at filling $\nu = 1/m$ are adiabatically exchanged counterclockwise in two dimensions.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Exchanging two Laughlin quasiholes generates a fractional Berry phase $\theta = \pi/m$ (so a full braid yields $2\theta = 2\pi/m$), establishing Abelian anyonic statistics intermediate between bosons ($\theta = 0$) and fermions ($\theta = \pi$).
formulas.intuitive_summary: Swapping two fractional quasiholes in a two-dimensional Laughlin fluid rotates the quantum wavefunction by a fraction $\pi/m$ of a half-turn, making them neither bosons nor fermions but anyons.
formulas.interpretation: Arovas, Schrieffer, and Wilczek computed the adiabatic Berry phase for transporting one quasihole in a closed loop encircling a second quasihole in $\Psi_m$, finding an Aharonov-Bohm background term plus a path-independent topological shift of $2\pi/m$; halving this full braid gives the single-exchange phase $\theta = \pi/m$. Because the fundamental group of two-dimensional configuration space is the braid group rather than the permutation group, this fractional phase is topologically quantized and immune to local deformations of the exchange path.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Originates from the one-dimensional Abelian unitary representations of the planar Artin braid group $B_N$ combined with the Chern-Simons topological field theory at level $k = m$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: At $m = 1$, $\theta = \pi$ reproduces ordinary fermionic exchange antisymmetry. In non-Abelian states such as the Moore-Read Pfaffian at $\nu = 5/2$, scalar phase multiplication generalizes to non-commuting unitary matrices acting on a degenerate subspace.

\\theta.name: Statistical Exchange Phase
\\theta.description: Topological phase angle acquired by the quantum state under a single counterclockwise interchange of two identical quasiholes.

\\pi.name: Pi
\\pi.description: Mathematical constant equal to the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.

m.name: Laughlin Odd Integer
m.description: Odd integer defining the primary Laughlin state at filling factor $\nu = 1/m$.

formulas.title: Composite-Fermion Effective Magnetic Field
formulas.description: Expresses the residual mean-field magnetic field $B^*$ experienced by composite fermions formed by attaching $2s$ magnetic flux quanta $\Phi_0$ to each electron of areal density $n$ in an external field $B$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Through Jain's flux-attachment transformation, attaching $2s$ quantized vortices to every electron absorbs an average flux density $2sn\Phi_0$ from the external field $B$, leaving weakly interacting composite fermions moving in a reduced effective field $B^* = B - 2sn\Phi_0$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Each electron swallows $2s$ magnetic flux quanta to become a composite fermion, canceling out most of the laboratory magnetic field so the new particles only feel the leftover field $B^*$.
formulas.interpretation: In Chern-Simons mean-field theory, replacing the singular attached flux tubes by a uniform smeared statistical magnetic field $-2sn\Phi_0$ reduces the strongly correlated fractional problem to nearly free fermions in field $B^*$. Because $B^*$ can be positive, zero, or negative depending on whether $B$ lies above, at, or below $2sn\Phi_0$, composite fermions execute cyclotron orbits of radius $R_c^* = \hbar k_F^*/(e|B^*|)$ that diverge as $B^* \to 0$ at even-denominator fillings $\nu = 1/(2s)$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived from the singular $U(1)$ Chern-Simons gauge transformation attaching $2s$ flux quanta per particle, which preserves fermionic exchange statistics while shifting the canonical vector potential.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: When $B = 2sn\Phi_0$ (filling $\nu = 1/(2s)$, notably $\nu = 1/2$ for $s = 1$), $B^* = 0$ and composite fermions form a gapless Fermi sea. When $s = 0$ (no flux attachment), $B^* = B$ recovers bare electrons in the external magnetic field.

B^*.name: Effective Composite-Fermion Magnetic Field
B^*.description: Residual mean-field magnetic flux density governing the cyclotron dynamics and Landau-like $\Lambda$-level quantization of composite fermions.

B.name: External Magnetic Field
B.description: Applied laboratory magnetic field perpendicular to the two-dimensional electron gas.

s.name: Flux-Attachment Pair Index
s.description: Positive integer such that $2s$ magnetic flux quanta (vortices) are bound to each electron.

n.name: Two-Dimensional Electron Density
n.description: Areal carrier density of electrons (and identically of composite fermions) in the two-dimensional plane.

\\Phi_0.name: Magnetic Flux Quantum
\\Phi_0.description: Fundamental quantum of magnetic flux $h/e$ attached in even multiples to each electron.

formulas.title: Jain Composite-Fermion Filling-Factor Sequence
formulas.description: Maps an integer number $p$ of filled composite-fermion $\Lambda$ levels in the effective field $B^*$ to the primary observed odd-denominator fractional quantum Hall filling factors $\nu = p/(2sp \pm 1)$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Jain's sequence $\nu = p/(2sp \pm 1)$ unifies the dominant odd-denominator fractional quantum Hall plateaus as integer quantum Hall states ($\nu^* = \pm p$) of composite fermions carrying $2s$ attached flux quanta.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Filling $p$ whole energy levels of composite fermions in their reduced magnetic field automatically produces the famous fractional plateaus $1/3, 2/5, 3/7, \dots$ and $2/3, 3/5, 4/7, \dots$ for the underlying electrons.
formulas.interpretation:
Setting the composite-fermion filling factor $
u^* = n\Phi_0 / B^* = \pm p$ and substituting $B^* = B - 2sn\Phi_0$ gives $B/(n\Phi_0) - 2s = \pm 1/p$, whose reciprocal yields $
u = p/(2sp \pm 1)$. For $s = 1$ (two attached flux quanta), the plus branch generates $1/3, 2/5, 3/7, 4/9, \dots$ converging to $
u = 1/2$ from below, while the minus branch generates $1, 2/3, 3/5, 4/7, \dots$ converging to $
u = 1/2$ from above; $s = 2$ similarly generates the series around $
u = 1/4$ ($1/5, 2/9, 3/13, \dots$).
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from the exact flux-attachment correspondence between electron density $n$, external magnetic flux $B/\Phi_0$, and integer $\Lambda$-level occupation $\nu^* = \pm p$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: At $p = 1$ on the plus branch, $\nu = 1/(2s + 1)$ reproduces the entire primary Laughlin sequence ($1/3, 1/5, 1/7, \dots$). As $p \to \infty$, both branches converge symmetrically onto the even-denominator composite-fermion Fermi sea at $\nu = 1/(2s)$.

\\nu.name: Electronic Filling Factor
\\nu.description: Observed fractional Landau-level filling factor of the physical two-dimensional electron gas.

p.name: Composite-Fermion Landau Level Index
p.description: Positive integer counting the number of completely filled composite-fermion $\Lambda$ levels in the effective field $B^*$.

s.name: Flux-Attachment Pair Index
s.description: Positive integer indicating that $2s$ magnetic flux quanta are bound to each electron.
